chapter: Leaving New York, jazz styles and religion
title: Baby brother's death on the road with Ray Charles
summary: His baby brother died while Smith's band toured with Ray Charles in 1952, which made him slow down.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: Well, I had lost my Dad in '40. And in '52, my baby brother was playing with me, a piano player.
I thought he was a bass player.
No. My baby brother was a piano player.
Oh, you had three other brothers.

I had four other brothers. Three of them are still living. But the one that played bass, he was next to the baby boy, (?), and the baby boy played piano. They could play piano. But Posey(?)/Jose(?), he couldn't play no piano. He played bass. So they let him stay on that bass. But... With Ray Charles.
Yeah. I had my band. It was my band, with Ray Charles. Ray Charles, he hit the circuit. We went all through

Arkansas, Louisiana, Oklahoma and all of Texas. And we was down in San Anton, and he went to go play that night, and somebody brought me a telegram. I forget now who it was, but anyhow they brought me a telegram, that my baby brother fell dead. Right down over there on (?) Street.

See, he was already kind of ill. But we didn't need him along with us, because Ray Charles was playing the piano, see -- so we didn't need him with the group. So we had six pieces. I had Cooper and Fathead. They was all in my band. So Ray had that tour, and he wanted me to make up the six pieces, just have six pieces along, and we played them dates. So we had to come back through here and go to Tulsa and play the next night. I come on home... I made it back. And then we were going to lay off for a week or so, so I was here for the funeral. But it made me start thinking. I was already thinking in the first place. But I thought, 'I'd better slow down, get on the other side of the fence.' Take it easy.
And you've stayed with it ever since.
